title: Nested Frames & Action Tiling — PRD Exploration (streaming + SDK ergonomics)
content:
Purpose:
This document explores a compact, latency-oriented approach to delivering incremental model output together with deterministic action frames (tool calls / structured outputs) across mobile and server SDKs. We call the pattern 'nested frames + action tiling' — the goal is to reduce perceived latency for interactive flows while preserving deterministic commit semantics for downstream tool execution and client-side replay.

Problem statement:
- Developers want first-token streaming for conversational and code assistants but also need precise, replayable tool invocations (e.g., search, DB ops, external API calls).
- Existing streaming designs either (a) stream raw tokens and post-process for actions (brittle and non-deterministic), or (b) buffer until a full structured action is ready (high latency).
- Mobile clients and low-bandwidth edge proxies require small, incremental checkpoints and clear client contract for partial vs committed results.

Goals (success criteria):
1) Latency: deliver usable incremental updates (text deltas + partial action hints) within 50–150ms of generation for short tokens in 90th percentile on standard networks.
2) Determinism: action commits (tool calls) are explicit, idempotent, and replayable.
3) SDK ergonomics: minimal cognitive overhead for client implementers — a few clear primitives to handle frames, commit events, and backpressure.
4) Observability: per-frame telemetry that ties user-facing latency to token generation, tool resolution time, and network layer.

Non-goals:
- Solving full multi-model orchestration (this is about a single-request streaming surface with tool call handshakes).
- Replacing long-term session storage/archival flows; checkpoints are short-lived and intended for resume/continue, not permanent indexing.

Design overview:
- Core idea: partition responses into hierarchical frames: a shallow sequence of textual microframes (immediate partial tokens), followed by zero-or-more action tiles (structured hints), and punctuated by an explicit Commit frame when an action is executed or final structured output is produced.
- Frames are small, self-describing envelopes transported over the existing streaming channel (HTTP/2/WS/Server-sent events). Each frame carries: id, parent_id (optional), type (microtext | action_hint | action_commit | checkpoint), sequence_index, and a compact prognostic checksum for lightweight client-side validation.

Frame types and semantics:
- microtext: cheap token deltas (partial text) that are non-authoritative. Client should render progressively but mark as tentative.
- action_hint: partial parsed structure (e.g., {"tool":"search","query":"..."}) emitted as soon as the model signals an intent to call a tool. Hints are advisory and may change in later frames.
- action_commit: authoritative tool invocation — idempotent, contains final structured args, a commit id, and optional out-of-band routing hints (region, variant). Once received, SDKs must surface this as a committed action and may optionally trigger automatic tool adapters.
- checkpoint: a compact snapshot (session token, kv-hash) that allows resumable sessions when clients reconnect. Checkpoints can be emitted periodically or at commit boundaries.

SDK ergonomics (proposed primitives):
- StreamClient.subscribe(onFrame) — low-level primitive that yields frames as they arrive. Frames are typed and documented.
- Renderer.renderTentative(textDelta) — helper that accepts microtext and handles cursor merging and light reflows.
- ActionCoordinator.onActionHint(hint) — optional callback for early UI affordances (preview buttons) without execution.
- ActionCoordinator.onActionCommit(commit) -> returns ActionResolution (auto|manual|defer). If auto, the SDK triggers a configured adapter (e.g., local search) with idempotency guarantees.
- StreamClient.requestResume(checkpoint) — resume flow using checkpoint.

Backpressure and network considerations:
- Clients can supply a preferred microframe cadence via handshake header (X-Downstream-Granularity: fast|balanced|coalesce). Server will adapt batching and microframe emission frequency during the session.
- For low-bandwidth clients, server can compress subsequent microtext frames relative to last-ack'ed checksum to reduce payload.

Idempotency and safety model for action_commit:
- commit_id (uuid) + sequence_index ensures replay safety. Server marks commit as durable once persisted in internal ledger; SDKs must surface commit-only once commit_id is received.
- For sensitive actions, ActionCommit can contain a required flag requiring developer confirmation (manual confirmation flows).

Observability and telemetry hooks:
- Emit per-frame events to Console: frame_received, render_latency, action_commit_latency, checkpoint_written. Tag events with model, region, request_profile, and client_bandwidth_class.
- Add a small token-count accounting field on frames for more accurate cost attribution in the Console.

Compatibility and migration path:
- Backwards-compatible: existing streaming clients that only render token stream continue to receive microtext frames concatenated into tokens. The new action frames are structured JSON envelopes; older clients will ignore unknown envelope types but may treat them as noise — to avoid breaking clients, the server will include a boolean 'legacy_friendly' header that toggles action frames into an embedded inline-text comment mode for legacy apps during a 3-month migration window.
- Migration stages: feature-flag rollout -> Beta SDKs (JS, Python) with adapters -> Telemetry opt-in -> Gradual default on (4 weeks).

Operational rollout and gating:
- Phase 0: internal integration tests with mock adapters (2 sprints). Focus on idempotency proofs and edge case replay tests.
- Phase 1: invite-only Beta with selected customers (3–6 integrations). Collect SDK ergonomics feedback and failure modes.
- Phase 2: public SDKs, opt-in by header. Monitor commit latencies and user-visible regressions.
- Phase 3: enable by default with migration helpers and console tooling to replay partial sessions.

Security and compliance notes:
- ActionCommits containing PII or sensitive fields must support field-level redaction tokens and be excluded from long-term telemetry by default.
- For Private/Dedicated customers, commit ledger persists to customer-owned stores where required.

Open questions and trade-offs:
- Where do we draw the line between an action_hint and a microtext that contains structured JSON inside prose? (heuristics vs model-supplied signals)
- Client-side UX: how aggressive should automatic execution be on action_hints? Default for first-party SDKs could be conservative (manual) and allow opt-in auto-execution.
- Checkpoint frequency: trade cost vs resume granularity. Proposed default: checkpoint every N=8 commits or at 10s intervals.

Next steps (immediate):
1) Engineering spike (serving-runtime): implement frame envelope and cost-aware microframe bundling in the streaming runtime (owner: Marco Li).
2) SDK spike (devexp): JS + mobile pseudocode for primitives and one reference adapter (owner: Ben Cho).
3) Product: prepare Beta invite list and sample prompts that exercise nested frames (owner: Asha Patel).
4) Security: draft redaction contract for committed frames (owner: Priya Nair).

Appendix — example minimal frame sequence (illustrative):
1) microtext(id=1, seq=1): "Sure — I can look up the latest pricing..."
2) action_hint(id=2, parent=1): {"tool":"catalog_search","query":"gpu-rtx pricing"}
3) microtext(id=3, seq=2): "…looks like the current best option is the rtx-6000…"
4) action_commit(id=4, parent=2, commit_id=uuid-1234): {"tool":"catalog_search","args":{"q":"gpu-rtx pricing","filters":{"region":"us-east-1"}}, "execute":true}
5) checkpoint(id=5): {"session_v":"3","kv_hash":"abc123"}

This draft is intentionally exploratory — looking for feedback on developer ergonomics, failure semantics, and where to draw defaults. Please add reactions inline or push comments to the linked Confluence page.
